A major controversy has emerged over ethanol blending in petrol after the Karnataka government claimed that fuel samples collected from multiple districts contained ethanol levels significantly above India's permitted E20 limit.
According to the state government, laboratory tests found ethanol content ranging from 25% to over 31% in samples linked to major oil marketing companies. Karnataka has raised concerns about fuel quality, vehicle performance and consumer transparency, while demanding mandatory disclosure of ethanol percentages at petrol pumps.
